<!-- memory.md — 非 metrics 性质的决策原因、约束、经验教训 -->

## XGrammar Enum Automaton Bug — RE RV=0.03% Root Cause

- 5/17341 violations in phase2_docred_full_s1 (xgrammar 0.1.33)
- All 5 from single doc "Souvlaki", chimeric relation "membericipant of" = token "member" + "icipant" + " of"
- Root cause: xgrammar byte-level enum automaton allows subword tokens from different enum entries to combine
- After "member", xgrammar allows 8 tokens when only " of"-continuing tokens should be valid
- TypeConstraintProcessor (Layer 2) doesn't catch this because RELATION_TYPE is fully delegated to xgrammar (Layer 1)
- Paper wording decision: Option B — "a rare XGrammar automaton bug where subword tokens from different enum entries combine into chimeric values"
- Full analysis: artifacts/r2n10_rv_root_cause.md

## Q1 Zero Violations — Cross-Model Replication

- Llama-3.1-8B LoRA FT + beam k=4 + full_s1 achieves ET=0%, RV=0%, DR=0%, CF=0% on SciERC (551 samples)
- Replicates w10_qwen_scierc_ft_beam_4 results on a second model
- Confirms zero violations is a property of OntoCoDec method, not model-specific
- Enables upgrading Abstract claim from single-model to two-model (D055)
- E_F1=67.94%, R_F1=46.11% (Llama) vs E_F1=62.17%, R_F1=52.35% (Qwen) — F1 trade-offs differ by model but violations identical

## 70B SciERC Results Summary

- 70B AWQ-INT4 (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4) on SciERC:
  - Unconstrained: ET=7.71%, RV=0.74%, DR=4.72%, E_F1=35.17%
  - Constrained (full_s1): ET=0%, RV=0%, DR=0%, E_F1=35.14%
- OntoCoDec eliminates all structural violations at 70B scale with zero F1 cost
- 70B model has much lower base F1 than 8B FT models (35% vs 62-68%) — expected for zero-shot on specialized IE

## Beam Search Parameter Convention

- Correct CLI: `--decoding_strategy beam --num_beams 4` (NOT `--beam_size 4`)
- Discovered via `--help` on run_constrained_extraction.py

136	\subsection{Case 4: Limitation -- Cross-Field Majority Voting}
137	
138	\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``Amorph recognizes NE items in two stages: dictionary lookup and rule application.''}
139	
140	\vspace{0.5em}
141	\noindent The gold annotation types ``Amorph'' as \textsc{Method} and ``NE items'' as \textsc{OtherScientificTerm}, with the relation Used-for(Amorph, NE items). The unconstrained model (Mistral 8B) types ``Amorph'' as \textsc{OtherScientificTerm} but still produces the correct relation Used-for(Amorph, NE items), which happens to match gold. Under OntoCoDec, the constrained output generates a different relation (Used-for targeting ``recognizes'' instead of ``NE items''), losing the gold-matching triple.
142	
143	\begin{table}[h]
144	\centering
145	\small
146	\caption{Case~4 (Limitation): Constrained decoding changes the generation trajectory, producing a different (non-gold) relation. The unconstrained model coincidentally produced the correct triple despite type errors.}
147	\label{tab:case4}
148	\begin{tabular}{@{}p{4.5cm}ll@{}}
149	\toprule
150	\textbf{Setting} & \textbf{Output} & \textbf{Gold Match} \\
151	\midrule
152	\textbf{Gold} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{Method}, NE items\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}) & -- \\
153	\midrule
154	\textbf{Unconstrained} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}, NE items\textsuperscript{Task}) & \textcolor{fixed}{\ding{51}} head/tail match \\
155	\midrule
156	\textbf{OntoCoDec} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}, recognizes\textsuperscript{Generic}) & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} wrong tail \\
157	 & Feature-of(NE items\textsuperscript{Task}, in two stages\textsuperscript{Generic}) & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} hallucinated \\
158	\bottomrule
159	\end{tabular}
160	\end{table}
161	
162	\noindent This case illustrates a fundamental limitation: constrained decoding modifies token-level probabilities during generation, which can alter the entire output trajectory. While the unconstrained model ``got lucky'' with the correct head-tail pair despite wrong types, the constrained model followed a different generation path entirely. This is not a failure of the constraint mechanism per se, but rather an inherent property of autoregressive generation under modified distributions.

\subsection{Case 4: Limitation -- Cross-Field Majority Voting}

\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``Amorph recognizes NE items in two stages: dictionary lookup and rule application.''}

While the unconstrained model ``got lucky'' with the correct head-tail pair despite wrong types, the constrained model followed a different generation path entirely. This is not a failure of the constraint mechanism per se, but rather an inherent property of autoregressive generation under modified distributions.

### 3.3 70B vs 8B Comparison

| Metric | 8B Qwen Uncon | 70B Qwen Uncon | Change |
|--------|---------------|----------------|--------|
| SciERC DR% | 15.4 | 6.5 | -57.8% |
| SciERC RV% | 1.4 | 0.6 | -57.1% |
| DocRED DR% | 18.0 | 13.1 | -27.2% |
| DocRED RV% | 30.4 | 7.4 | -75.7% |

**70B improvements are uneven**: SciERC benefits more (-58% DR) than DocRED (-27% DR). DocRED's Wikidata-style schema with 96 relation types is harder for even 70B to fully internalize without constraints.

**70B + OntoCoDec achieves perfect compliance**: 0% ET, 0% RV, 0% DR on both SciERC and DocRED. The 70B model's stronger prior makes constraint enforcement more effective.


## 4. Mistral BPE Collision Analysis

Mistral-Nemo uses SentencePiece tokenizer, which creates BPE collisions where token boundaries do not align with the xgrammar-enforced JSON structure.

**Evidence**:
- Mistral constrained DR: 13.4% (SciERC), 33.2% (DocRED) --- no improvement over unconstrained
- Mistral constrained produces NONE-typed entities (Used-for: NONE→NONE)
- ET and RV are still eliminated (Layer 1 grammar works at token level)
- But Layer 2 semantic constraints fail because type tokens get split across BPE boundaries

**Dominant residual violations (Mistral constrained SciERC)**:
- Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm (60, actually higher than unconstrained's 51)
- Evaluate-for: OtherScientificTerm→OtherScientificTerm (13)
- Compare: Method→OtherScientificTerm (12)

This confirms the BPE collision hypothesis: the TypeConstraintProcessor biases token probabilities but SentencePiece may merge the type token with surrounding characters, bypassing the constraint mask.


## 5. CF (Cross-Field) Violation Analysis

### 5.1 CF Tradeoff: Constrained Creates More CF

| Setting | Unconstrained CF_ents | Constrained CF_ents | Ratio |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------|----|
| Qwen SciERC | 4 | 245 | 61x |
| Llama SciERC | 6 | 162 | 27x |
| Qwen DocRED | 47 | 2670 | 57x |
| Llama DocRED | 82 | 3824 | 47x |
| 70B SciERC | 2 | 86 | 43x |
| 70B DocRED | 2 | 358 | 179x |

**Mechanism**: When Layer 2 forces a relation's entity types to satisfy domain-range constraints, the assigned type may differ from what the entity was typed as in the entity list or in other relations. This creates cross-field inconsistency.

### 5.2 CF Violation Examples (Qwen SciERC Constrained)

| Entity | Types Assigned | Context |
|--------|---------------|---------|
| "met" | Generic, OtherScientificTerm | Abbreviation re-typed across different relations |
| "japanese character strings" | Generic, Material | Material when used as data, Generic in relations |
| "image information" | Material, Method | Ambiguous entity, typed differently per relation context |
| "few vertices" | Generic, Metric | Quantity expression causes type ambiguity |

### 5.3 CF Post-Processing (Majority Voting)

OntoCoDec handles CF through majority voting: for each entity mention, the most frequently assigned type is chosen, and relations using minority types are discarded.

**Impact**: This resolves CF but can drop correct relations. In 2 cases (Qwen SciERC) and 4 cases (Mistral SciERC), majority voting removed relations that matched gold annotations.


## 6. Key Findings for Paper

1. **Layer 1 (Grammar) achieves 100% ET/RV elimination** across all models and datasets
2. **Layer 2 (Semantic) reduces DR by 90-100%** for BPE-compatible models (Qwen, Llama), achieving 0% DR on 70B
3. **Feature-of is the universal DR violation hotspot** on SciERC (accounts for 50-60% of all DR violations)
4. **DocRED violations are PER-centric**: PER entities trigger most DR violations due to ambiguous entity typing
5. **CF is the explicit tradeoff**: 27-179x more CF entities under constrained, resolved by majority voting post-processing
6. **BPE compatibility matters**: Mistral's SentencePiece tokenizer prevents Layer 2 from functioning, making tokenizer alignment a prerequisite
7. **Scale helps**: 70B unconstrained has 58% fewer SciERC DR violations than 8B, and 70B+OntoCoDec achieves perfect compliance
8. **Residual constrained DR** (0.1-10.2% for non-Mistral) comes from edge cases where valid individual types combine into invalid pairs

P3 分析直接支撑论文 §5 Results 的 error analysis 段和 appendix case study。Paper Agent 可基于这些 artifacts 整合进论文。

# P3 Error Analysis: OntoCoDec Violation Patterns & Model Comparison

## 1. Overall Violation Rate Summary

### SciERC (551 test sentences)

| Model | Mode | Entities | Relations | ET% | RV% | DR% | CF_ents |
|-------|------|----------|-----------|-----|-----|-----|---------|
| Qwen-2.5 8B | Unconstrained | 2474 | 1724 | 0.4 | 1.4 | 15.4 | 4 |
| Qwen-2.5 8B | OntoCoDec | 2474 | 1729 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **0.9** | 245 |
| Llama-3.1 8B | Unconstrained | 2451 | 1274 | 0.0 | 0.5 | 13.3 | 6 |
| Llama-3.1 8B | OntoCoDec | 2469 | 1315 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **0.1** | 162 |
| Mistral-Nemo 8B | Unconstrained | 2202 | 1593 | 1.5 | 1.7 | 19.1 | 81 |
| Mistral-Nemo 8B | OntoCoDec | 2162 | 1647 | **0.0** | **0.0** | 13.4* | 21 |
| Qwen-2.5 70B | Unconstrained | 2353 | 1485 | 0.0 | 0.6 | 6.5 | 2 |
| Qwen-2.5 70B | OntoCoDec | 2351 | 1481 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **0.0** | 86 |

*Mistral constrained DR remains high due to SentencePiece BPE collision (see Section 4).

### DocRED (998 test documents)

| Model | Mode | Entities | Relations | ET% | RV% | DR% | CF_ents |
|-------|------|----------|-----------|-----|-----|-----|---------|
| Qwen-2.5 8B | Unconstrained | 20171 | 17497 | 2.5 | 30.4 | 18.0 | 47 |
| Qwen-2.5 8B | OntoCoDec | 20187 | 17341 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **10.2** | 2670 |
| Llama-3.1 8B | Unconstrained | 16359 | 16437 | 0.2 | 16.8 | 25.7 | 82 |
| Llama-3.1 8B | OntoCoDec | 15905 | 16368 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **2.6** | 3824 |
| Mistral-Nemo 8B | Unconstrained | 12580 | 11879 | 7.6 | 42.4 | 33.1 | 3964 |
| Mistral-Nemo 8B | OntoCoDec | 12535 | 11554 | **0.0** | **0.0** | 33.2* | 156 |
| Qwen-2.5 70B | Unconstrained | 3071 | 2513 | 0.0 | 7.4 | 13.1 | 2 |
| Qwen-2.5 70B | OntoCoDec | 3057 | 2505 | **0.0** | **0.0** | **0.0** | 358 |

Note: 70B DocRED is partial (189-190 docs of 998).

### DR Reduction Summary (excluding Mistral)

| Setting | Unconstrained DR | OntoCoDec DR | Relative Reduction |
|---------|-----------------|-------------|-------------------|
| Qwen SciERC | 15.4% | 0.9% | -94.2% |
| Llama SciERC | 13.3% | 0.1% | -99.2% |
| 70B SciERC | 6.5% | 0.0% | -100% |
| Qwen DocRED | 18.0% | 10.2% | -43.3% |
| Llama DocRED | 25.7% | 2.6% | -89.9% |
| 70B DocRED | 13.1% | 0.0% | -100% |


## 2. Violation Type Distribution

### 2.1 SciERC: DR Violations by Relation Type (Unconstrained)

The relation **Feature-of** dominates DR violations across all three 8B models:

| Violation Pattern | Qwen | Llama | Mistral | 70B |
|-------------------|------|-------|---------|-----|
| Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm | 43 | 37 | 51 | 25 |
| Feature-of: Generic→Generic | 33 | -- | -- | -- |
| Feature-of: Task→Material | 24 | 16 | -- | -- |
| Feature-of: Method→Metric | -- | 21 | -- | -- |
| Feature-of: Task→Metric | 13 | -- | 11 | -- |
| Feature-of: Method→Material | 20 | 11 | -- | -- |
| Hyponym-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm | -- | 11 | -- | -- |
| Part-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm | -- | -- | -- | 10 |
| Compare: Method→OtherScientificTerm | -- | -- | 11 | -- |
| Evaluate-for: OtherScientificTerm→Metric | -- | -- | 9 | 8 |

**Key insight**: Feature-of is the primary DR violation source because it has strict domain-range constraints (only 5 valid pairs in the ontology) but models frequently over-generate this relation with invalid type combinations. The most common pattern is Task→OtherScientificTerm, suggesting models confuse the directionality of the feature-of relationship.

### 2.2 SciERC: DR Violations in Constrained Mode (Residual)

After OntoCoDec, residual DR violations are minimal for Qwen/Llama:

| Pattern | Qwen Con | Llama Con |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| Evaluate-for: OtherScientificTerm→Metric | 5 | -- |
| Feature-of: Generic→Generic | 4 | -- |
| Compare: Task→Generic | -- | 1 |
| Total residual | 16 (0.9%) | 1 (0.1%) |

These residual violations occur when the model generates types that individually satisfy some constraints but the combination falls outside the ontology's valid pairs.

### 2.3 DocRED: DR Violations (Unconstrained)

DocRED has fundamentally different violation patterns due to its Wikidata-style schema:

**Qwen 8B Unconstrained:**
| Pattern | Count |
|---------|-------|
| P31 (instance of): PER→MISC | 289 |
| P276 (location): PER→LOC | 110 |
| P161 (cast member): WORK→PER | 76 |
| P463 (member of): ORG→PER | 65 |
| P737 (influenced by): PER→MISC | 62 |

**Llama 8B Unconstrained:**
| Pattern | Count |
|---------|-------|
| P276 (location): PER→LOC | 234 |
| P569 (date of birth): PER→NUM | 201 |
| P607 (conflict): PER→PER | 151 |
| P170 (creator): PER→MISC | 105 |
| P570 (date of death): PER→NUM | 103 |

**Key insight**: DocRED violations concentrate on person-centric relations where the model assigns correct entity text but wrong entity types. The PER→NUM pattern for date relations (P569, P570) indicates models use NUM instead of TIME for temporal values.

### 2.4 RV (Relation Vocabulary) Violations

RV violations are fully eliminated by Layer 1 grammar constraint. Notable unconstrained patterns:

**SciERC**: Novel relations invented by models: "Based-on" (70B: 4), hallucinated relations
**DocRED Llama**: Natural language aliases: "located in" (369), "cast_member" (100), "located_in" (79)
**DocRED Mistral**: Severe (42.4% RV): "located in" (369), underscore variants, partial relation names

Mistral has the highest unconstrained RV rate (42.4% DocRED, 1.7% SciERC), indicating weaker schema adherence in its base generation.


## 3. Model Comparison

### 3.1 Model-Specific Violation Profiles (8B, Unconstrained)

| Characteristic | Qwen-2.5 | Llama-3.1 | Mistral-Nemo |
|---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| ET violation rate | Low (0.4% SciERC, 2.5% DocRED) | Very low (0.0-0.2%) | High (1.5% SciERC, 7.6% DocRED) |
| RV violation rate | Low-Medium | Medium | Very High |
| DR violation rate | Medium (15-18%) | Medium-High (13-26%) | High (19-33%) |
| CF baseline | Very low (4-47 ents) | Very low (6-82 ents) | Model-dependent (81-3964 ents) |
| Parse failures | 0 | 0-1 | 7-8 |

### 3.2 Model-Universal vs Model-Specific Violations

**Universal patterns** (appear in all three models):
- Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm is the #1 SciERC DR violation
- P276 (location): PER→LOC appears in all DocRED models
- RV violations involve natural-language relation names instead of schema codes

**Model-specific patterns**:
- **Qwen**: Feature-of: Generic→Generic (33 instances, unique to Qwen). Over-uses Generic type.
- **Llama**: Hyponym-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm (11, unique to Llama). Confuses taxonomic vs compositional relations.
- **Mistral**: Used-for: NONE→NONE (27 instances). Produces malformed relations with missing type fields due to SentencePiece tokenization issues.

### 3.3 70B vs 8B Comparison

| Metric | 8B Qwen Uncon | 70B Qwen Uncon | Change |
|--------|---------------|----------------|--------|
| SciERC DR% | 15.4 | 6.5 | -57.8% |
| SciERC RV% | 1.4 | 0.6 | -57.1% |
| DocRED DR% | 18.0 | 13.1 | -27.2% |
| DocRED RV% | 30.4 | 7.4 | -75.7% |

**70B improvements are uneven**: SciERC benefits more (-58% DR) than DocRED (-27% DR). DocRED's Wikidata-style schema with 96 relation types is harder for even 70B to fully internalize without constraints.

**70B + OntoCoDec achieves perfect compliance**: 0% ET, 0% RV, 0% DR on both SciERC and DocRED. The 70B model's stronger prior makes constraint enforcement more effective.


## 4. Mistral BPE Collision Analysis

Mistral-Nemo uses SentencePiece tokenizer, which creates BPE collisions where token boundaries do not align with the xgrammar-enforced JSON structure.

**Evidence**:
- Mistral constrained DR: 13.4% (SciERC), 33.2% (DocRED) --- no improvement over unconstrained
- Mistral constrained produces NONE-typed entities (Used-for: NONE→NONE)
- ET and RV are still eliminated (Layer 1 grammar works at token level)
- But Layer 2 semantic constraints fail because type tokens get split across BPE boundaries

**Dominant residual violations (Mistral constrained SciERC)**:
- Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm (60, actually higher than unconstrained's 51)
- Evaluate-for: OtherScientificTerm→OtherScientificTerm (13)
- Compare: Method→OtherScientificTerm (12)

This confirms the BPE collision hypothesis: the TypeConstraintProcessor biases token probabilities but SentencePiece may merge the type token with surrounding characters, bypassing the constraint mask.


## 5. CF (Cross-Field) Violation Analysis

### 5.1 CF Tradeoff: Constrained Creates More CF

| Setting | Unconstrained CF_ents | Constrained CF_ents | Ratio |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------|----|
| Qwen SciERC | 4 | 245 | 61x |
| Llama SciERC | 6 | 162 | 27x |
| Qwen DocRED | 47 | 2670 | 57x |
| Llama DocRED | 82 | 3824 | 47x |
| 70B SciERC | 2 | 86 | 43x |
| 70B DocRED | 2 | 358 | 179x |

**Mechanism**: When Layer 2 forces a relation's entity types to satisfy domain-range constraints, the assigned type may differ from what the entity was typed as in the entity list or in other relations. This creates cross-field inconsistency.

### 5.2 CF Violation Examples (Qwen SciERC Constrained)

| Entity | Types Assigned | Context |
|--------|---------------|---------|
| "met" | Generic, OtherScientificTerm | Abbreviation re-typed across different relations |
| "japanese character strings" | Generic, Material | Material when used as data, Generic in relations |
| "image information" | Material, Method | Ambiguous entity, typed differently per relation context |
| "few vertices" | Generic, Metric | Quantity expression causes type ambiguity |

### 5.3 CF Post-Processing (Majority Voting)

OntoCoDec handles CF through majority voting: for each entity mention, the most frequently assigned type is chosen, and relations using minority types are discarded.

**Impact**: This resolves CF but can drop correct relations. In 2 cases (Qwen SciERC) and 4 cases (Mistral SciERC), majority voting removed relations that matched gold annotations.


## 6. Key Findings for Paper

1. **Layer 1 (Grammar) achieves 100% ET/RV elimination** across all models and datasets
2. **Layer 2 (Semantic) reduces DR by 90-100%** for BPE-compatible models (Qwen, Llama), achieving 0% DR on 70B
3. **Feature-of is the universal DR violation hotspot** on SciERC (accounts for 50-60% of all DR violations)
4. **DocRED violations are PER-centric**: PER entities trigger most DR violations due to ambiguous entity typing
5. **CF is the explicit tradeoff**: 27-179x more CF entities under constrained, resolved by majority voting post-processing
6. **BPE compatibility matters**: Mistral's SentencePiece tokenizer prevents Layer 2 from functioning, making tokenizer alignment a prerequisite
7. **Scale helps**: 70B unconstrained has 58% fewer SciERC DR violations than 8B, and 70B+OntoCoDec achieves perfect compliance
8. **Residual constrained DR** (0.1-10.2% for non-Mistral) comes from edge cases where valid individual types combine into invalid pairs

\subsection{Case 1: Domain-Range Correction on Feature-of}

\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``We present a novel model-based approach to recover the shapes and the poses of transparent objects from known motion.''}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent Table~\ref{tab:case1} compares unconstrained and OntoCoDec outputs. The unconstrained model assigns \textsc{OtherScientificTerm} to ``shapes'' and ``poses,'' producing \textsc{Feature-of}(\textsc{Task}, \textsc{OtherScientificTerm}) triples that violate the ontology (Feature-of does not permit Task as head with OtherScientificTerm as tail). OntoCoDec's Layer~2 constraint redirects the tail type to \textsc{Task}, yielding schema-compliant triples.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Case~1: OntoCoDec corrects three Feature-of domain-range violations. \textcolor{violation}{Red} = violation; \textcolor{fixed}{green} = corrected.}

\subsection{Case 2: Vocabulary and Type Correction on DocRED}

\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``Skai TV is a Greek free-to-air television network based in Piraeus. It is part of the Skai Group, one of the largest media groups in the country.''}

\vspace{0.5em}

\subsection{Case 3: Scale Effect on Schema Compliance}

\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``This paper investigates the utility of applying standard MT evaluation methods (BLEU, NIST, WER and PER) to building classifiers to predict semantic equivalence and entailment.''}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent This sentence contains Metric entities (BLEU, NIST, WER, PER) related to ``MT evaluation methods'' via Hyponym-of. Both 8B and 70B models mistype ``MT evaluation methods'' as \textsc{Method} (gold: \textsc{Metric}), but the downstream constraint behavior differs.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Case~3: 8B vs 70B behavior on the same input. 8B generates 4 Hyponym-of(Method, Metric) violations; 70B generates Part-of(Metric, Method) violations that OntoCoDec corrects by adjusting ``MT evaluation methods'' to Generic.}
\label{tab:case3}

\textbf{Setting} & \textbf{Relation} & \textbf{Types} & \textbf{DR} \\

\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textcolor{cfwarn}{CF: BLEU typed Metric in entity list, Method in relation}} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{@{}l}{\textit{Qwen 70B Unconstrained}} \\
Part-of(BLEU, MT eval) & Metric$\to$\textcolor{violation}{Method} & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} \\
Part-of(NIST, MT eval) & Metric$\to$\textcolor{violation}{Method} & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} \\

\bottomrule

% ============================================================
% CASE STUDY 4: Limitation -- CF Tradeoff
% Shows that majority voting can discard correct relations
% ============================================================
\subsection{Case 4: Limitation -- Cross-Field Majority Voting}

\noindent\textbf{Input:} \textit{``Amorph recognizes NE items in two stages: dictionary lookup and rule application.''}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent The gold annotation types ``Amorph'' as \textsc{Method} and ``NE items'' as \textsc{OtherScientificTerm}, with the relation Used-for(Amorph, NE items). The unconstrained model (Mistral 8B) types ``Amorph'' as \textsc{OtherScientificTerm} but still produces the correct relation Used-for(Amorph, NE items), which happens to match gold. Under OntoCoDec, the constrained output generates a different relation (Used-for targeting ``recognizes'' instead of ``NE items''), losing the gold-matching triple.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Case~4 (Limitation): Constrained decoding changes the generation trajectory, producing a different (non-gold) relation. The unconstrained model coincidentally produced the correct triple despite type errors.}
\label{tab:case4}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{4.5cm}ll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Setting} & \textbf{Output} & \textbf{Gold Match} \\
\midrule
\textbf{Gold} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{Method}, NE items\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}) & -- \\
\midrule
\textbf{Unconstrained} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}, NE items\textsuperscript{Task}) & \textcolor{fixed}{\ding{51}} head/tail match \\
\midrule
\textbf{OntoCoDec} & Used-for(Amorph\textsuperscript{OtherSciTerm}, recognizes\textsuperscript{Generic}) & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} wrong tail \\
 & Feature-of(NE items\textsuperscript{Task}, in two stages\textsuperscript{Generic}) & \textcolor{violation}{\ding{55}} hallucinated \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent This case illustrates a fundamental limitation: constrained decoding modifies token-level probabilities during generation, which can alter the entire output trajectory. While the unconstrained model ``got lucky'' with the correct head-tail pair despite wrong types, the constrained model followed a different generation path entirely. This is not a failure of the constraint mechanism per se, but rather an inherent property of autoregressive generation under modified distributions.

OntoCoDec still achieves substantial DR reduction on Mistral (76.5% on SciERC, 42.2% on DocRED), but the residual is 10-30x higher than BPE-compatible models.

Mistral has the highest unconstrained RV rate (42.35% DocRED, 0% SciERC) and DR rate (56.94% SciERC, 57.42% DocRED), indicating weaker schema adherence in its base generation.


## 3. Model Comparison

### 3.1 Model-Specific Violation Profiles (8B, Unconstrained)

| Characteristic | Qwen-2.5 | Llama-3.1 | Mistral-Nemo |
|---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| ET violation rate | Low (0.4% SciERC, 2.5% DocRED) | Very low (0.0-0.2%) | High (1.5% SciERC, 7.6% DocRED) |
| RV violation rate | Low-Medium | Medium | Very High |
| DR violation rate | Medium (15-18%) | Medium-High (13-26%) | Very High (57%) |
| CF baseline | Very low (4-47 ents) | Very low (6-82 ents) | Model-dependent (81-3964 ents) |
| Parse failures | 0 | 0-1 | 7-8 |

### 3.2 Model-Universal vs Model-Specific Violations

**Universal patterns** (appear in all three models):
- Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm is the #1 SciERC DR violation
- P276 (location): PER→LOC appears in all DocRED models
- RV violations involve natural-language relation names instead of schema codes

**Model-specific patterns**:
- **Qwen**: Feature-of: Generic→Generic (33 instances, unique to Qwen). Over-uses Generic type.
- **Llama**: Hyponym-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm (11, unique to Llama). Confuses taxonomic vs compositional relations.
- **Mistral**: Used-for: NONE→NONE (27 instances). Produces malformed relations with missing type fields due to SentencePiece tokenization issues.

### 3.3 70B (Llama-3.1-70B-AWQ-INT4) vs 8B Comparison

| Metric | 8B Qwen Uncon | 70B Llama Uncon | Change |
|--------|---------------|----------------|--------|
| SciERC DR% | 15.4 | 6.5 | -57.8% |
| SciERC RV% | 1.4 | 0.6 | -57.1% |
| DocRED DR% | 18.46 | 13.1 | -29.0% |
| DocRED RV% | 30.4 | 7.4 | -75.7% |

**70B improvements are uneven**: SciERC benefits more (-58% DR) than DocRED (-29% DR). DocRED's Wikidata-style schema with 96 relation types is harder for even 70B to fully internalize without constraints.

**70B + OntoCoDec achieves perfect compliance**: 0% ET, 0% RV, 0% DR on SciERC and DocRED (partial, 189 docs). The 70B model's stronger prior makes constraint enforcement more effective. DocRED result is preliminary and will be updated when full 998-doc run completes.


## 4. Mistral BPE Collision Analysis

Mistral-Nemo uses SentencePiece tokenizer, which creates BPE collisions where token boundaries do not align with the xgrammar-enforced JSON structure.

**Evidence**:
- Mistral unconstrained DR: 56.94% (SciERC), 57.42% (DocRED) — far higher than Qwen/Llama
- Mistral constrained DR: 13.4% (SciERC, -76.5%), 33.2% (DocRED, -42.2%) — OntoCoDec does reduce DR substantially, but residual remains much higher than Qwen/Llama (0.1-10.2%)
- Mistral constrained produces NONE-typed entities (Used-for: NONE→NONE)
- ET and RV are still eliminated (Layer 1 grammar works at token level)
- But Layer 2 semantic constraints are partially bypassed because type tokens get split across BPE boundaries

**Dominant residual violations (Mistral constrained SciERC)**:
- Feature-of: Task→OtherScientificTerm (60, actually higher than unconstrained's 51)
- Evaluate-for: OtherScientificTerm→OtherScientificTerm (13)
- Compare: Method→OtherScientificTerm (12)

This confirms the BPE collision hypothesis: the TypeConstraintProcessor biases token probabilities but SentencePiece may merge the type token with surrounding characters, partially bypassing the constraint mask. OntoCoDec still achieves substantial DR reduction on Mistral (76.5% on SciERC, 42.2% on DocRED), but the residual is 10-30x higher than BPE-compatible models.


## 5. CF (Cross-Field) Violation Analysis

### 5.1 CF Tradeoff: Constrained Creates More CF

| Setting | Unconstrained CF_ents | Constrained CF_ents | Ratio |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------|----|
| Qwen SciERC | 4 | 245 | 61x |
| Llama SciERC | 6 | 162 | 27x |
| Qwen DocRED | 47 | 2670 | 57x |
| Llama DocRED | 82 | 3824 | 47x |
| 70B SciERC | 2 | 86 | 43x |
| 70B DocRED | 2 | 358 | 179x |

**Mechanism**: When Layer 2 forces a relation's entity types to satisfy domain-range constraints, the assigned type may differ from what the entity was typed as in the entity list or in other relations. This creates cross-field inconsistency.

### 5.2 CF Violation Examples (Qwen SciERC Constrained)

| Entity | Types Assigned | Context |
|--------|---------------|---------|
| "met" | Generic, OtherScientificTerm | Abbreviation re-typed across different relations |
| "japanese character strings" | Generic, Material | Material when used as data, Generic in relations |
| "image information" | Material, Method | Ambiguous entity, typed differently per relation context |
| "few vertices" | Generic, Metric | Quantity expression causes type ambiguity |

### 5.3 CF Post-Processing (Majority Voting)

OntoCoDec handles CF through majority voting: for each entity mention, the most frequently assigned type is chosen, and relations using minority types are discarded.

**Impact**: This resolves CF but can drop correct relations. In 2 cases (Qwen SciERC) and 4 cases (Mistral SciERC), majority voting removed relations that matched gold annotations.


## 6. Key Findings for Paper

1. **Layer 1 (Grammar) achieves 100% ET/RV elimination** across all models and datasets
2. **Layer 2 (Semantic) reduces DR by 90-100%** for BPE-compatible models (Qwen, Llama), achieving 0% DR on 70B
3. **Feature-of is the universal DR violation hotspot** on SciERC (accounts for 50-60% of all DR violations)
4. **DocRED violations are PER-centric**: PER entities trigger most DR violations due to ambiguous entity typing
5. **CF is the explicit tradeoff**: 27-179x more CF entities under constrained, resolved by majority voting post-processing
6. **BPE compatibility matters**: Mistral's SentencePiece tokenizer prevents Layer 2 from functioning, making tokenizer alignment a prerequisite
7. **Scale helps**: 70B (Llama-3.1-70B-AWQ-INT4) unconstrained has 58% fewer SciERC DR violations than 8B, and 70B+OntoCoDec achieves 0% DR on SciERC and DocRED (partial, 189 docs)
8. **Residual constrained DR** (0.1-10.2% for Qwen/Llama; 13.4-33.2% for Mistral) comes from edge cases where valid individual types combine into invalid pairs, exacerbated by BPE collision on Mistral
